provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The factory is the previous one, unchanged. In visible coordinates it does the following:
1. Background is palette[0]. The structural colour is the most common non-background colour.
2. Shapes are 8-connected multicolour components of size greater than 1 that contain the structural colour. Every other non-background cell is a loose target marker.
3. For each shape it lists every distinct placement under the 8 D4 matrices. A placement is a symmetry plus a translation that puts all of the shape's embedded markers on loose markers of the same colours.
4. The matrices are conjugated by the episode's d4 as G M G^-1. The generator's own four transforms (vertical flip, transpose, the two quarter-turns) are tried first, then the remaining four.
5. It backtracks to find an assignment in which no two shapes use the same marker.
6. It erases the original shapes and stamps each one at its assigned placement.
No grid is rotated or recoloured.

The host failure was not a factory bug. It came from an ambiguous synthetic scene. The repair is in the constructor:
- The deterministic drawing code moves unchanged into _render, so all explicit fixture inputs and outputs are reproduced exactly.
- Random sampling becomes bounded: there are caps on placement retries and on marker-position retries, and a cap on the number of scenes tried.
- Each sampled scene must pass _unambiguous before it is returned.

_unambiguous works only from the visible input and does not depend on any solver's search order:
- The structural colour must be the strict most common colour, and must equal the generator's mode.
- Each sprite must appear intact, be 8-connected, and have no foreign non-background cell in its 8-neighbourhood. This means the shape and target split is the same under 4- or 8-connectivity.
- Loose markers must not contain the structural colour.
- It enumerates every placement of every sprite under all 8 symmetries and all translations, keyed by the full stamped cell set. Out-of-bounds stamps are counted too, which is the conservative choice.
- It counts complete assignments with disjoint marker use and accepts the scene only if there is exactly one.

This test is D4-invariant, so it holds under every host augmentation. When it passes, the unique assignment must be the generated one, which makes the label the unique visible answer.
draft_notes.limitations:
Nothing has been run. I am assuming the following about the generator's helpers:
- common.grids fills with background 0.
- common.random_colors(4) does not return 0.
- continuous_creature returns (row, col) pixels.
- common.overlaps keeps the bounding squares at least 3 apart. The isolation check rejects any scene where this fails visibly.

Distribution changes:
- Two-sprite scenes with an ambiguous assignment are rejected. These are mainly scenes where the two marker triples are congruent under D4, plus rare cross-triple coincidences. This removes a modest fraction of two-sprite scenes.
- num_sprites is drawn once per call, so its distribution is unchanged except in the practically unreachable case where 400 scenes in a row fail. Only then does sampling fall back to one sprite. If that also fails 400 times, generate raises instead of looping forever.
- Scenes that the original sampler would have looped on forever (for example a perfectly straight creature) are now abandoned and resampled.

The factory still contains a greedy last-resort fallback for inputs outside this domain. It is never reached on accepted scenes.
draft_notes.diagnosis:
The failure is on train pair 1 of the fresh episode (d4=0; palette gives background 7, structural colour 9, markers 3, 2 and 4). That input has two complete, non-overlapping, in-bounds solutions:

| Shape | Markers relative to its 3 | Fits set 1 by | Fits set 2 by |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (rows 2-5, cols 13-15) | 4 at (-1,0), 2 at (0,1) | vertical flip | rotation (y,x)->(x,-y) |
| B (rows 6-7, cols 2-6) | 2 at (-1,0), 4 at (0,1) | rotation (y,x)->(x,-y) | vertical flip |

The two loose triples are:
- Set 1: 3 at (12,11), 2 at (12,12), 4 at (13,11), so 2 at (0,1) and 4 at (1,0).
- Set 2: 3 at (15,3), 4 at (15,4), 2 at (16,3), so 4 at (0,1) and 2 at (1,0).

Set 1 and set 2 are mirror images of each other, and so are A's and B's triples. All four transforms in the table are among the generator's rotates 1-4. The label uses A→set 2 and B→set 1, both by rotation. The factory, which tries vertical flip first, returned A→set 1 and B→set 2, both by flip. The archived solver also takes A→set 1. Nothing in the input or the demonstrations separates the two answers. The other three checks in the episode passed. The previous factory is therefore correct on unambiguous scenes. Changing its tie-break to reproduce this label would be fitting a hidden latent.
draft_notes.constructor_issue:
The random branch of generate() samples the three marker positions of each sprite independently. It never checks that the visible input determines the sprite-to-legend assignment. When two sprites' coloured marker triples are congruent under D4 (here, mirror-image L-trominoes), each sprite fits each clone triple. Two different outputs are then equally consistent with the input, and the label is fixed by the hidden latents rotates[i] and the sprite-to-clone pairing, which no solver can recover.

The sampler also has unbounded while-loops: the overlap placement loop, and the marker pick loop, which never ends if a creature is a straight line.

The proposed constructor rejects such scenes with an exhaustive check over all 8 symmetries that counts complete assignments, and bounds all loops. The canonical fixtures are not changed: their inputs and outputs come from the same _render code. Each fixture shape there has a unique match, so I see no fixture contradiction. The repair requires host review and execution before it is applied.
draft_notes.host_review: Explicit fixture inputs/outputs compared exactly to canonical source before applying. No smaller-object-count fallback allowed; exhaustion raises.
